fp-01-alegria.context: Paul writes from prison, unsure if he will leave alive. Some preach Christ even from twisted motives, and the church in Philippi prays for him. Even so, the letter's tone is joy, not complaint.
fp-01-alegria.focusQuestion: What would still be joy for you if everything else were taken away?
fp-01-alegria.keywordGloss: In Paul, joy does not depend on circumstances: it comes from Christ being proclaimed and exalted.
facts: Paul rejoices as long as Christ is proclaimed, by pretext or by truth.
He expects deliverance thanks to the church's prayer and the Spirit's provision.
Christ will be exalted in Paul's body, by life or by death.
For Paul, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
He desires to depart and be with Christ, which is incomparably better.
He judges it more necessary to stay in the flesh for the church's sake.

fp-02-humildade.context: Paul wants a united church, without rivalry or vanity. For that, he does not give only an order: he shows the path of Christ himself, who descended from God to servant and to the cross.
fp-02-humildade.focusQuestion: In what relationship do you need to stop defending yourself and start serving?
fp-02-humildade.keywordGloss: The mind of Christ: instead of clinging to what is his, he empties himself and serves to the end.
facts: Paul asks the church to share the same mind and be united in soul.
With humility, each one must consider others superior to himself.
Each one must also care for what is others', not only his own.
Christ, existing in the form of God, did not cling to being equal with God.
He emptied himself, taking the form of a servant.
He humbled himself, obedient unto death, even death on a cross.

fp-03-contentamento.context: Paul gives thanks because the Philippians began helping him financially again, after a time without opportunity. Before they think he depends on money to be well, he explains what he learned.
fp-03-contentamento.focusQuestion: What would change if what you have today were enough for you?
fp-03-contentamento.keywordGloss: It is not resignation: it is living whole in plenty and in lack, strengthened by Christ.
facts: Paul rejoiced because the Philippians finally remembered him.
He learned to live content in every and any situation.
He knows what it is to be brought low and also to be honored.
He has already had experience of plenty and hunger, abundance and scarcity.
He can do all things through the one who gives him strength.
The Philippians sent help twice when he was in Thessalonica.

fp-04-desafio.context: This challenge reviews the whole letter: imprisoned Paul's joy, the mind of Christ who became a servant, and contentment learned in plenty and in lack. Three themes, one center.
fp-04-desafio.focusQuestion: Which of the three themes — joy, humility, or contentment — do you most need to live today?
fp-04-desafio.keywordGloss: Joy in prison, descent to servant, and strength in lack: in Philippians, everything turns on Christ.
facts: Paul rejoices as long as Christ is proclaimed, even in prison.
For Paul, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
Christ emptied himself, taking the form of a servant.
God exalted Christ and granted him the name above every name.
Paul learned to live content in every and any situation.
He can do all things through the one who gives him strength.
